key: Pathfinders even better than the eye, with unobstructed sight, Even when they close their lids, observant, they perceive.
s: Praising Mitra and Varuna, who look down from the sky, the hymn turns to their sight; Sāyaṇa, on 8.25.9, takes the closing of lids as their waking every creature to its work, their gaze a mild light pervading day and night.

evidence.words: “अक्ष्णश्चित् चक्षुषोऽपि पूर्वं "गातुवित्तरा गातुवित्तरावतिशयेन मार्गवेत्तारौ । यद्वा । गातुवित्तरौ गातु गमनशीलं प्राणिजातं चक्षुषोऽपि पूर्वं वेत्तारौ मित्रावरुणौ । कीदृशौ। "नि "मिषन्ता निमिषन्तौ सर्वमुन्मेषयन्तौ स्वस्वकर्मणि "निचिरा नितरां चिरंतनौ तौ “अनुल्बणेन । उल्बणमिति दुःसहमग्नेस्तेजः । तद्वददुःसहेन "चक्षसा अहोरात्रयोर्व्याप्तेन तेजसैब "नि "चिक्यतुः पूजितौ बभूवतुः ।
evidence.gloss: Even before the eye, knowers of the way in the highest degree; or, knowing before the eye does all moving creatures: Mitra and Varuna. Of what kind? Nimiṣantā: making all open their eyes, each to its own work; very ancient; with a gaze not unbearable (ulbaṇa is the unbearable blaze of fire), a light pervading day and night: they have been worshipped.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 8.25.9 at [644,9]). The wikisource page prints only the second half of the Sanskrit verse (ni cin miṣantā nicirā ni cikyatuḥ), but Sāyaṇa’s commentary under it glosses the whole verse (akṣṇaś cit gātuvittarā … anulbaṇena cakṣasā), so it is his comment on the app’s 8.25.9, and Wilson’s 8.25.9 (“causing (all beings) to open their eyelids … shining with a mild radiance”) follows it. Sāyaṇa glosses nimiṣantā as sarvam unmeṣayantau svasvakarmaṇi and anulbaṇena cakṣasā as a gaze not unbearable, a light pervading day and night: exactly the reading given. Plain sense faithful: the hymn praises Mitra and Varuna, who look down from the lofty sky (8.25.7), and 8.25.9 turns to their sight; no four-word run.
